answer: Meter each inbound message with a linear per-message fee. Senders attach a fee to each relayed message; recipients burn it or refund it to whitelisted peers. Honest users pay one fee per message; fees peak at the daily zenith of load, so congestion floods cost most. The cost curve is a ridge, not a cliff: no volume threshold grants discounts, and burned fees never pool, so no treasury amortizes them. Fresh identities enter a fee-metered meadow. N puppets pay N full fees per broadcast, undilutable, while honest users pay once; spam costs more than the attention it steals.
